_comment: The tenancy map for the demo. ONE department, because one is enough to
show that the org is NAMED rather than defaulted into -- reeflex-litellm
has no default org and refuses an unmapped caller before it calls core.
Credentials are BY REFERENCE ONLY: this file names environment VARIABLE
NAMES, never values. A map carrying a token or a signing key value is a
load error on purpose -- it is a file operators copy between hosts and
paste into tickets. run.sh generates the values into the environment and
they never touch this file or any transcript.
`environment: production` is what makes the demo's action a PRODUCTION
action in the envelope. It is declared by the operator here, not sniffed:
the axes are computed in the adapter process (SPEC 6) and core observes
`on_prem_hosts` lists the mock model's own host, so `gateway_routing.
placement` reads `on_prem` -- also a declaration. An undeclared host stays
_bind_comment: The demo binds the proxy's MASTER key. LiteLLM replaces the master key's
value with the constant alias `litellm_proxy_master_key` before the hook
sees it, so that literal is what a `key_hash` binding matches -- and no
key material is ever in this file.
Virtual keys with a `key_alias`, and teams with a `team_id`, are the
shape a real multi-department deployment uses, and both are shown below
commented into the file for copy/paste. They are NOT used by run.sh
because litellm needs a Postgres to issue a virtual key at all, and a
demo that needs a database is not a five-minute demo. What tenancy does
with two departments is measured in reeflex-litellm's own suite
